design_choice_and_rationale.chosen_mechanism: Reuses the summary_index / summary_rev mechanism merged in REGISTRY-SUMMARY-PAGE-NO-RESCAN-20261127 instead of introducing a second cache design: stored column lineage_index JSONB on registry.entries (holding the 14 pre-projected flat lineage fields for every object entry row) shares the existing summary_rev BIGINT column, sequence pantheon_registry_summary_rev_seq, and BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF payload trigger entries_strategy_summary_index_tg (pantheon_registry_summary_index_tg_fn calling pantheon_registry_summary_index_build and pantheon_registry_lineage_index_build), plus partial index entries_lineage_index_idx (ON registry.entries (summary_rev ASC) WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL) and idempotent bounded batched backfill at store bootstrap (LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE = 1000, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, leaving updated_at unchanged), paired with a single-flight in-process stamp-validated compiled adjacency cache (_CompiledLineageRowList / _CompiledLineageGraphIndex, bounded to LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16 tenant views) validated on every read by one cheap aggregate query (SELECT count(*), coalesce(max(summary_rev), 0)::bigint, coalesce(sum(summary_rev), 0)::bigint FROM registry.entries WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL) and updated incrementally in O(degree) time after writes via partial index entries_lineage_index_idx (WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL AND summary_rev > %s).
why_both_stored_columns_and_incremental_: 1. Eliminates per-request full-table payload detoasting and 14 JSON path evaluations in PostgreSQL: storing the pre-projected ~410.4-byte lineage_index JSONB and shared 8-byte summary_rev BIGINT on registry.entries drops Postgres lineage read buffer hits on 9,944 hosted-shape rows (9,418 strategy_spec, 344 execution_bundle, 182 alpha_template) from 114,607 shared buffers / 712.06 ms (legacy payload scan with 2x CTE evaluation) down to 2,881 shared buffers / 59.48 ms on a cold stored-column scan, 2,881 shared buffers / 4.81 ms on a warm stamp query, and 6 shared buffers / 0.101 ms on a post-write 1-row delta index scan.

2. Eliminates per-request full-population Python JSON decoding and adjacency graph reconstruction: even with stored lineage_index columns, decoding 9,944 rows and rebuilding all node dictionaries, family indices, and edge maps on every request across 8 concurrent cold reads without an in-process cache takes 16,244.52-28,424.18 ms wall time and 866.95-910.03 MiB peak RSS (+777.52-820.59 MiB delta). With the single-flight stamp-validated compiled adjacency cache (_CompiledLineageGraphIndex) and incremental O(degree) delta updates, 8 concurrent cold reads on a fresh process collapse to 1 SQL load + 1 adjacency build + 7 cache hits: wall time drops from 11,509.03-22,332.28 ms to 2,007.74-3,809.58 ms (3.0x-6.6x faster) and peak RSS (VmHWM) drops from 460.61-541.42 MiB (+371.24-452.08 MiB delta) to 216.19-216.71 MiB (+126.81-127.33 MiB delta, 66-72% lower memory delta, well within DEV_MEM_LIMIT_REGISTRY=768m). Subsequent warm reads complete in 21.71-25.01 ms end-to-end.

3. Immediate write visibility and single unified cache invalidation design: reusing summary_rev and entries_strategy_summary_index_tg means every write path (create_if_absent, put, _cas_entry, create_with_receipt, register_strategy_spec_revision, update_metadata, advance_artifact_state, or writes from another process sharing Postgres) atomically advances summary_rev and updates both summary_index and lineage_index in the same BEFORE trigger; on the next read, the stamp query detects the revision change, fetches only the modified rows via WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL AND summary_rev > %s, and incrementally splices old/new edges in _CompiledLineageGraphIndex.apply_delta_rows.

sql_lineage_reads.stamp_query: SELECT count(*), coalesce(max(summary_rev), 0)::bigint, coalesce(sum(summary_rev), 0)::bigint FROM registry.entries WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL
sql_lineage_reads.full_load_query: SELECT record_id, summary_rev, lineage_index FROM registry.entries WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL ORDER BY updated_at ASC, record_id ASC
sql_lineage_reads.delta_load_query: SELECT record_id, summary_rev, lineage_index FROM registry.entries WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL AND summary_rev > %s ORDER BY updated_at ASC, record_id ASC

runtime_budget.manifest_entry_name: registry.entries stored lineage_index / summary_rev columns, partial index entries_lineage_index_idx, and stamp-validated incremental lineage adjacency cache
runtime_budget.cadence: DDL and idempotent batched backfill run once at store bootstrap; shared trigger entries_strategy_summary_index_tg runs once per registry.entries INSERT or UPDATE OF payload (~300 writes/day on hosted); stamp validation query runs once per GET /api/registry/lineage read (4.8 ms); delta index query runs only for rows with summary_rev > cached_max_rev
runtime_budget.growth_per_day: about 300 new rows/day x (410.4 B lineage_index + ~24 B partial index tuple; summary_rev already shared with summary_index) = ~130 KB/day (~47 MB/year); 0 B net logical growth on in-place updates after VACUUM; 0 B/day net in-process cache growth beyond the entry set and LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16 cap
runtime_budget.cap: 1 lineage_index JSONB (~410 B) and 1 shared summary_rev BIGINT (8 B) per object row in registry.entries; bootstrap backfill bounded by LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE = 1000 and LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_MAX_BATCHES = 50; in-process lineage tenant view + adjacency cache bounded to LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16 with FIFO eviction
runtime_budget.cleanup: stored columns and partial index tuples follow registry.entries row lifecycle with PostgreSQL VACUUM; non-object rows set lineage_index = NULL via trigger; in-process cache evicts oldest tenant view beyond LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16, updates existing adjacency views incrementally on stamp change or evicts stale views on delete/retire, and supports full eviction via invalidate_lineage_index_cache(full=True)

rollback_compatibility.mechanism: lineage_index and summary_rev are nullable columns maintained by BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF payload trigger entries_strategy_summary_index_tg; the previous release's INSERT/UPDATE statements only touch (record_id, payload, updated_at) and SELECT statements only read (record_id, payload, updated_at) or (record_id, summary_rev, summary_index), which continue to succeed without error while the trigger keeps both summary_index and lineage_index current
